result.decision_rationale:
The Windows build and package records establish the 0.31.1 baseline for the measured DLL. Changes are required because packaging can still accept stale or misattributed artifacts, a valid ZIP can be rejected, and the supported IDE path lacks execution evidence.

Continuation for Claude

Bind receipt reuse to the effective build configuration and resolved references. Use one typed receipt for candidate admission and export, and derive the ZIP digest from the same archive inspected for DLL metadata. Move the build-output replacement into the disposable test harness and validate directory markers by their decoded contents. Exercise these corrections through the ordinary package, candidate and standalone validation paths.

Supply the IDE observation from an authorized environment or keep that evidence gap open. Move full logs out of the tracked tree, retain portable qualification records, complete the owner Harmony inventory and align the current summaries with the tested commit and case count. Limit corrections to Dice Roller tooling, focused tests and current documentation. The native rows can retain their documented NOT RUN disposition.

executed_verification: The controller domain gate passed 416/416 at 444d58ba12a351281a2d0e4e8d42decffbbd927f. I verified its log digest against the receipt.
I ran the repository's read-only Python source validator at the submitted snapshot and git diff --check across the feature change. Both passed. All 14 exported evidence digests matched their index.

The recorded clean Windows Build-Local run at fca7cdef06dd28805b356fdd8ad78356b21fc800 passed 20 release-gate checks, 30 Python cases, 416 domain cases and the Kingmaker, respec and native-UI contract checks. The production compiler command names both pinned files and reports zero warnings and errors.

The build receipt, package records and API audit agree on DLL SHA-256 634f22775c62bb34461fb202d85ab9d088f4e1cb1bd062e959812c8bcf9b12ee. The archived DLL has MVID 7a6d0a75-f788-47a5-83c9-fed6fb14e3ff and references UnityModManager 0.31.1.0 and 0Harmony12 1.2.0.1. The recorded ZIP SHA-256 is b8cb456b8061fc48bfa464bd5af66f368516ab24cbb22d3d1f2c6e376d436e81.

All 75 recorded boundary cases matched their log entries. They include genuine v0.2.0 manifest-only rejection, both validation orders in one Windows PowerShell host, receipt checks and the disposable installer dry run.

The static audit records seven types and 25 members with zero unresolved references on 0.31.1, 0.32.4, owner 0.33.0 and 0.33.4 using the same DLL. The packet includes the auditor source and dated newest-stable selection.
An independent in-memory Python zipfile check produced a genuine empty directory record with five compressed bytes and zero decoded bytes at DEFLATE level zero.
inspected: Mission, repository instructions, full feature diff, correction commits, developer report, transcript withholding notice, controller receipt and all eight pending ledger items.

Production project, MSBuild targets, reference verifier, build receipt, package and installation scripts, their qualification callers, boundary tests, compatibility documentation and evidence exports.

The 16 files changed between the measured build commit and the submitted commit are all documentation or evidence. Production sources, build scripts and packaged files are identical across those commits.
limitations: The foreground tool transcript was withheld. The domain run has a controller receipt at the submitted commit. The Windows build, boundary suite and static audit were assessed from the supplied execution records.
The build-host inventory shows Visual Studio Build Tools only. Its incremental MSBuild results do not observe the IDE's up-to-date decision.

Native roll and assignment, fresh-process persistence, mercenary, respec and combined-stack behavior are untested on all four loaders. The mission permits this disposition given the unavailable disposable harness.
required_gaps: Effective build-input binding, consistent receipt and ZIP identity, and regression evidence for those package paths.
Removal of the production test mutation and acceptance of a valid compressed empty directory marker.
An IDE-originated trace covering an otherwise up-to-date project and a loader-contract-only change.
Repository-compliant evidence storage, complete owner runtime identity and consistent current qualification records.
source_inspection_only: The conditional managed-directory mismatch follows from comparing the PowerShell XML reader with the production project's MSBuild import.

The candidate receipt reread and the gap between closing the inspected archive and hashing its path were established by source inspection. The recorded suite changes the build DLL after staging and does not exercise either interval.

findings.actual: Get-BuildInputFingerprint hashes literal HintPaths under the first directory returned by Get-KingmakerConfiguration. MSBuild evaluates the complete GamePath.props import. A later Release override can therefore direct compilation to directory B while the receipt continues to hash directory A. The new byte-change test exercises a single unconditional directory.
findings.blocking_rationale: A change to a reference actually used by the Release compiler can leave the receipt fingerprint unchanged and allow reuse of the previous DLL.
findings.expected: The fingerprint describes the effective inputs for the selected production configuration.
findings.requested_correction: Use the evaluated production configuration and resolved reference identities for the fingerprint, or enforce a single supported configuration interpretation for both compilation and receipt validation.
findings.requested_evidence: In a temporary checkout, select a different Managed directory for Release, show which file the compiler resolves, and demonstrate stale-receipt rejection when that file changes. Preserve acceptance for identical reference bytes relocated elsewhere.
findings.title: Receipt reuse can hash a different Managed directory from the compiler
findings.trigger: GamePath.props supplies a default Managed directory and overrides it for the Release configuration.

findings.actual: Package.ps1 freezes the receipt at lines 14–16, then reopens build-provenance.json at line 25 for its clean-commit check. With byte-identical builds on successive commits, the second receipt can pass admission while the manifest and exported receipt name the first commit. The producing commit and dirty fields also receive no scalar type validation.
findings.blocking_rationale: A directory labeled as an exact clean candidate can contain a producing receipt that never passed the exact-commit check.
findings.expected: Candidate admission checks the producing commit and Boolean dirty state on the same validated receipt bytes that the package exports.
findings.requested_correction: Validate producer identity and dirty-state types on the frozen receipt. Use that object for the candidate guard and the manifest, and use the staged DLL for candidate version checks.
findings.requested_evidence: Show that a receipt from an earlier commit with identical DLL bytes cannot qualify as the current clean candidate, including when the on-disk receipt is refreshed during packaging. Include malformed producer metadata and a genuine passing control.
findings.title: Candidate admission checks a different receipt from the one it exports
findings.trigger: A rebuild refreshes the on-disk receipt between its initial read and the candidate clean-commit check.

findings.actual: The validator closes the inspected archive at line 109 and reopens PackagePath for its SHA-256 at line 141. A replacement in between gives the report the first archive's DLL identity and the second archive's digest. Package.ps1 now trusts that digest, so its final path-hash comparison can also pass.
findings.blocking_rationale: A successful validation record can identify ZIP bytes whose DLL was never inspected against the receipt.
findings.expected: The reported ZIP digest, DLL digest, MVID and AssemblyRefs all describe one immutable archive.
findings.requested_correction: Hash and inspect the same held file or private snapshot. Use that digest for the final published-path agreement check.
findings.requested_evidence: Use two independently identified benign archives in temporary storage. Show that the report always pairs a ZIP digest with that ZIP's DLL identity, or rejects the changed output.
findings.title: The ZIP digest is read after the validated archive is closed
findings.trigger: A supplied or generated ZIP is replaced after entry inspection and before the validation report is written.

findings.actual: The submitted trace invokes MSBuild /t:Build. The inventory establishes why an IDE trace was unavailable on this host. The repository still ships the Visual Studio solution and documents the IDE build path.
findings.blocking_rationale: The IDE can decide that a project is up to date before invoking MSBuild. The command-line runs cannot establish that this path reaches the guard.
findings.expected: An ordinary supported IDE build reaches the reference guard after a manifest-only or pin-only change.
findings.requested_correction: Capture the supported IDE path in an authorized environment. If that prerequisite remains unavailable, retain the gap in the handoff.
findings.requested_evidence: Provide an IDE-originated trace with an up-to-date control, guard rejection after a loader-contract-only change, and acceptance after restoration.
findings.title: The Visual Studio up-to-date decision remains unobserved
findings.trigger: Build the otherwise up-to-date production project from the shipped solution after changing only a loader-contract input.

findings.actual: The production packaging script force-copies the file named by a test environment variable over artifacts/bin's compiled DLL. The recorded candidate test confirms successful packaging with the legacy DLL left in the build output until the harness restores it.
findings.blocking_rationale: The packaging entry point can destroy the reusable build output and leave its build receipt pointing to different bytes.
findings.expected: Packaging consumes the qualified build output. The disposable harness owns any deliberate replacement used to test concurrent changes.
findings.requested_correction: Remove the environment-driven overwrite from Package.ps1 and arrange the post-staging replacement entirely within the temporary test setup.
findings.requested_evidence: Retain the post-staging regression and show that ordinary packaging preserves its input DLL and receipt.
findings.title: A test hook in production packaging overwrites the compiled DLL
findings.trigger: Package.ps1 inherits the test replacement environment variable.

findings.actual: The new rule rejects any directory with CompressedLength greater than two. Python's standard ZIP writer produced an empty KingmakerDiceRoller/ record with compressed length five and decoded length zero. That legitimate record meets the rejection predicate.
findings.blocking_rationale: Standalone validation and installer preflight can reject an otherwise valid supplied baseline ZIP solely because of its compression encoding.
findings.expected: An allowed package directory with empty decoded content validates across valid ZIP encodings.
findings.requested_correction: Validate the allowed directory name and emptiness of its content without assuming a two-byte maximum compressed representation.
findings.requested_evidence: Run the standalone validator on a genuine six-file package with a level-zero DEFLATE empty directory record. Retain both existing nonempty-directory rejection cases.
findings.title: Valid compressed empty directories are rejected
findings.trigger: A supplied baseline ZIP contains an explicit package directory compressed at DEFLATE level zero.

findings.actual: The candidate tracks full build and boundary-suite logs. The audit wrapper retains an absolute fleet-workspace path at line 5. The compiler log and IDE inventory also retain absolute machine paths.
findings.blocking_rationale: AGENTS.md line 64 prohibits logs and local paths in Git. Renaming command output to .txt and replacing some path prefixes leaves that requirement unmet.
findings.expected: Tracked documentation provides portable qualification facts. Full execution logs are available through a permitted review evidence route.
findings.requested_correction: Remove the tracked logs and machine paths from the candidate tree. Preserve the reviewer-readable measurements in portable structured records and deliver any necessary full logs through the permitted evidence route.
findings.requested_evidence: Show a clean scan of the corrected tracked evidence and confirm that the review packet still exposes the compiler inputs, artifact identities and observed boundary results.
findings.title: The evidence export commits logs and machine-local paths
findings.trigger: Inspect the evidence directory introduced by the final documentation commit.

findings.actual: The owner row additionally lists 0Harmony-1.2 with only the digest prefix e6bf8079 and no assembly version. The machine audit identifies the three assemblies supplied to the static auditor. It provides no further identity for this installed component.
findings.blocking_rationale: The direct static results are reproducible, but the measured owner runtime record leaves one explicitly listed Harmony component unidentified.
findings.expected: The owner runtime record identifies the complete relevant Harmony stack and distinguishes it from the inputs selected for direct API inspection.
findings.requested_correction: Record the additional component's assembly identity and full SHA-256, or establish from the measured profile why it falls outside the relevant runtime stack.
findings.requested_evidence: Provide a dated, path-independent identity entry or the dependency evidence supporting its exclusion. The existing four direct API results can stand for their recorded inputs.
findings.title: The owner runtime inventory abbreviates an additional Harmony component
findings.trigger: Reconcile the measured owner installation with the three-component static audit profile.

findings.actual: The current qualification section still reports 58/58. The compatibility guide reports 75/75 on the candidate commit. The execution records identify fca7cde as the 75-case run and 444d58b as the later documentation commit with the controller domain receipt.
findings.blocking_rationale: The current qualification summaries give conflicting counts and obscure which validation actually ran at each revision.
findings.expected: Current documentation names the tested source, the observed case count and the basis for carrying frozen-artifact evidence across the documentation commit.
findings.requested_correction: Align the current qualification section and compatibility guide with the producing revision and controller gate receipt. Preserve the historical release sections.
findings.requested_evidence: The current summaries should agree with the source SHA, case count and artifact identities in the corresponding execution records.
findings.title: Current qualification summaries disagree on the boundary-suite run
findings.trigger: Compare PROJECT-STATE.md with the compatibility guide and recorded suite output.

prior_finding_assessments.rationale: Wrapper changes and byte changes under the simple Managed path now invalidate reuse. Ordinary packages also correctly distinguish producing and packaging commits. The fingerprint still follows a different configuration interpretation from MSBuild when a later property group selects the effective references.

The exact auditor source, four measured outputs, full identities for its three inputs per profile, frozen mod identity and dated newest-stable selection are now available. R3-F6 concerns the additional component named in the installed runtime inventory.

The recorded post-staging build-DLL replacement leaves the archived DLL, loose candidate DLL, manifest and exported receipt in agreement. R3-F1 concerns the earlier admission check. R3-F2 concerns the ZIP digest itself.
The host inventory and revised documentation accurately disclose the available tooling. They do not establish the supported IDE's up-to-date behavior or withdraw the mission requirement.

The production compiler command, contract results, receipt, package identities, genuine legacy rejection and both same-host validation orders are now reviewable. Git confirms that the subsequent evidence commit preserves the measured production and package inputs.

Private validation runs during WhatIf, and live installation changes remain behind ShouldProcess. The recorded real installer dry runs reached the disposable target for the valid ZIP, rejected the legacy ZIP and preserved the Mods and temporary directory state.

The hash, configuration and loader fields receive scalar checks before comparison. Ordinary packaging rejected the malformed fields, and standalone validation rejected an explicitly empty expected digest. The two-build cases separately established byte mismatch rejection.

Directory entries are checked before the six-file count. Both recorded nonempty-directory cases were rejected and the genuine package passed. R3-F4 covers a separate regression affecting genuinely empty records.

summary.delivered_behavior: Dice Roller declares UMM 0.31.1 and the measured production DLL uses the pinned UMM and Harmony12 references. The standalone validator rejects the genuine older release with only its manifest lowered. Four static loader profiles passed for the same DLL.
